# AI Coding Agent Worktree Usage

This reference covers how major AI coding tools use (or don't use) git worktrees for isolation and parallel execution.

For source details, see [citations.md](../citations.md).

## Tool Comparison

| Tool | Worktree Support | Isolation Model | Max Parallel | Release |
|------|-----------------|-----------------|--------------|---------|
| Claude Code | Native (`--worktree` flag) | Git worktree | No stated limit | v2.1.49+ [3] |
| Cursor | Native (automatic) | Git worktree | 20 per workspace [4] | 2.0 (Oct 2025) |
| Copilot CLI | Native (mode selection) | Git worktree or workspace | Not specified | 2026 [5] |
| Aider | No native support | None (manual worktrees) | N/A | [37] |
| OpenHands | No worktree support | Docker containers | Per container config | [discovery] |
| Devin | No worktree support | Full sandbox | Per sandbox config | [discovery] |
| SWE-agent | No worktree support | Commit reset | Per repo config | [discovery] |

## Claude Code

**Flag:** `--worktree` (`-w`) creates an isolated worktree at `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>/` with branch `worktree-<name>` [3].

**Base branch:** Branches from `origin/HEAD`. Not configurable via flag; use `git remote set-head origin -a` to re-sync, or configure a `WorktreeCreate` hook for full control [3].

**Cleanup behavior** [3]:
- No changes → worktree and branch removed automatically
- Changes/commits exist → Claude prompts to keep or remove

**Subagent isolation:** Custom subagents can specify `isolation: worktree` in frontmatter; each subagent gets its own worktree, auto-cleaned when finished without changes [3].

**Agent Teams:** Coordinated parallel sessions with shared tasks and messaging [3].

**`.worktreeinclude` file:** Lists gitignored files (e.g., `.env`, `.env.local`) to copy into new worktrees automatically. Uses `.gitignore` syntax [3].

**Hooks:** `WorktreeCreate` and `WorktreeRemove` hooks enable custom worktree logic, including non-git VCS support [3].

## Cursor

**Architecture:** "1:1 mapping of agents to worktrees" — each agent operates in its own isolated environment [4][23].

**Configuration:** `.cursor/worktrees.json` with platform-specific setup commands (`setup-worktree-unix`, `setup-worktree-windows`) [4].

**Limits:** "Per-workspace limit: Each workspace can have up to 20 worktrees." Oldest worktrees auto-removed by last access time. Default cleanup interval: 6 hours [4].

**Best-of-N ensemble mode:** Run "a single prompt on multiple models at once" to compare outputs and selectively apply the best result [4].

**Apply process:** (1) New/edited files from primary working tree are brought to worktree, (2) agent works in isolation, (3) clicking "Apply" merges changes back to primary working tree [4].

**Limitation:** "For performance reasons, Cursor currently does not support LSP in worktrees. The agent will not be able to lint files" [4].

## Copilot CLI (VS Code)

**Two isolation modes** [5][6]:

| Mode | Permission | Auto-commit | Use case |
|------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| Worktree | Bypass Approvals (fixed, cannot change) | Yes, end of each turn | "Hand off and walk away" [6] |
| Workspace | Configurable (3 tiers) | No | "Interactive experience" [6] |

Worktree isolation: "All changes made by the agent are applied to the worktree, keeping them separate from your main workspace" [5]. Requires Git repository [5].

**Auto-commit:** "The agent automatically commits changes to the worktree at the end of each turn, so the session history stays aligned with the commit history" [5].

**Gap:** Copilot proper (non-CLI) does not yet have worktree isolation modes [discovery].

## Aider

**No native worktree support.** GitHub Issue #302 documents problems with parallel Aider instances: log file overwrites, stale files, diff mixing [37].

**AiderDesk** (third-party GUI) has added worktree support including AI-powered conflict resolution for worktree rebase flows [38].

Users run Aider in worktrees via external tools like CodeRabbit's git-worktree-runner [28].

## Container-Based Tools (OpenHands, Devin, SWE-agent)

These tools use **container isolation** rather than git worktrees [discovery]:

- **OpenHands:** Docker containers with `DockerWorkspace` API; opt-in sandboxing with optional Daytona integration
- **Devin:** Fully sandboxed environments; developer out of the loop until review
- **SWE-agent:** Repository classes with commit reset behavior

## Three Isolation Paradigms

| Paradigm | Tools | Isolates | Does NOT isolate |
|----------|-------|----------|-----------------|
| Git worktrees | Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot CLI | Files, branches, staging | Ports, databases, Docker daemon [20] |
| Docker containers | OpenHands, Devin | Full environment | Host filesystem access |
| OS-level user isolation | Experimental ("walrus" pattern) | Filesystem permissions | Shared kernel resources |

Key limitation shared by all worktree-based tools: "if your app talks to a database, a cache, or a message queue, Git worktrees alone won't isolate those resources" [20].

## Gaps and Limitations

- **Exact Claude Code version and date for worktree release** could not be independently confirmed beyond "v2.1.49+" from secondary sources.
- **Aider's current stance** on native worktree support is unclear; Issue #302 age is unknown.
- **Disk usage at scale:** One report claims Cursor consumed 9.82 GB during a 20-minute session on a ~2GB codebase, but this is a single data point [discovery].
- **No quantitative merge conflict rate data** found for any tool's worktree workflows.
